def test_r11_dst_spring_forward_shifts_gap():
    # 2023-03-12 in America/New_York: clocks jump from 02:00 EST to 03:00 EDT.
    # 01:30:00 EST -> 03:30:00 EDT is only 1 hour of real time (3600 s),
    # not the 2 hours the naive wall-clock strings suggest.
    time_strings = ["2023-03-12 01:30:00", "2023-03-12 03:30:00"]
    assert task_func(time_strings, "America/New_York") == pytest.approx(3600.0)

def test_r12_dst_fall_back_shifts_gap():
    # 2023-11-05 in America/New_York: clocks fall back from 02:00 EDT to
    # 01:00 EST.  00:30:00 EDT -> 02:30:00 EST is 3 hours of real time
    # (10800 s), not the 2 hours the wall-clock strings suggest.
    time_strings = ["2023-11-05 00:30:00", "2023-11-05 02:30:00"]
    assert task_func(time_strings, "America/New_York") == pytest.approx(10800.0)

def test_r13_timezone_argument_is_used():
    # Same wall-clock strings, two different timezones: the mean gap must be
    # identical because both conversions shift all timestamps equally.
    time_strings = [
        "2023-07-01 12:00:00",
        "2023-07-01 12:00:05",
        "2023-07-01 12:00:15",
    ]
    utc_result = task_func(time_strings, "UTC")
    kolkata_result = task_func(time_strings, "Asia/Kolkata")
    assert utc_result == pytest.approx(5.0)
    assert kolkata_result == pytest.approx(5.0)
